S. Hughes and A. Zoelle (with M. Woods, S. Henry, S. Homsy, S. Pidaparti, N. Kuehn, H. Hoffman, K. Forrest, A. Sheriff, T. Fout, W. M. Summers, S. Herron, H. Mantripragada, P. Cvetic, E. Grol), "Cost of Capturing CO2 from Industrial Sources," National Energy Technology Laboratory, Pittsburgh, DOE/NETL-2023/3907, March 31, 2023. No DOI or URL printed.

LOADED (16 cases, all Dec-2018 USD): six high-purity compression-only cases (ammonia, ethylene oxide, ethanol, NGP, CTL, GTL; greenfield) and ten low-purity capture cases (refinery-hydrogen SMR ADIP-Ultra pre-combustion 90/99%; cement CANSOLV post-combustion 90/99% greenfield; iron/steel CANSOLV 90/99% retrofit; pulp mill CANSOLV 90/99% greenfield and retrofit). Per case: description, capacity (t CO2/yr at 100% CF, derived as printed CO2 captured at 85% CF / 0.85 except pulp where printed), annual-output (printed, 85% CF), capacity factor 85%, capture rate (low purity only), capex = TOC plant total (COST BASIS: overnight; from Exhibits 7-2 to 7-4), fixed O&M = annual $ total / capacity (formula), variable O&M $/t CO2 (summary tables), cost of capture (COC, cost-levelized, ex. T&S), capital charge factor (capital-recovery), electricity kWh/t from total auxiliary load, natural gas MMBtu/t for the regeneration-steam boiler (from the O&M fuel line). NOT LOADED (in _other-values.csv): TPC, BEC, TASC, owner's costs, COC components, retrofit COCs of greenfield cases (retrofit factor only), cement FGD+SCR sensitivity COCs, fixed charge rates, TASC/TOC ratios, prices, CO2 available and U.S. emissions by industry, pulp NG kg/h. Not transcribed: line-item capital cost tables, stream tables, plant-capacity and price sensitivity curves (figures only), integrated pulp/paper sensitivity, carbon balances (appendix). No abatement (avoided) cost is reported: the study reports cost of CO2 captured only, and boiler CO2 is not captured. Energy-for-steam in greenfield pulp is supplied by the base plant at zero cost (base-plant derate noted in the electricity row). No _flows.csv written: energy inputs are recorded as specific-energy-consumption.

(1) Exhibit 7-2 labels the ammonia representative plant size "394,000 tonnes EO/year" (should be ammonia).; (2) Normalisation of the O&M $/tonnes/yr columns is inconsistent: most cases divide fixed O&M by CO2 at 100% CF but variable O&M by CO2 at 85% CF (e.g. ammonia 3.28 and 2.67), pulp/paper divides fixed O&M by CO2 at 85% CF (12.74 = 10,704,098/840,334), and iron/steel divides all O&M and TOC ($627/t-yr, Exhibit 6-46) by ~1.85 Mt/yr, about half the 3.70 Mt/yr the two capture sections handle; fixed O&M was therefore recomputed from the $/yr totals.; (3) Text TOCs disagree with the exhibits: cement 90% greenfield "$386.0 M" (p.104) vs 394,192 k$ (Exhibits 6-22, 7-3); cement 99% "$424,897,000" (p.29) vs 413,960 k$; iron/steel retrofit "$1,151 M" and "$1,055 M" (p.130) vs 1,160,313 and 1,063,524 k$ (Exhibits 6-46, 7-3/7-4). Exhibit values used.; (4) Refinery hydrogen total power "4.01 MW and 4.42 MW" in text (p.89) vs 4,040 and 4,410 kWe in Exhibit 6-5; exhibit used.; (5) Exhibit 6-73 title says "1.3 M adt/year pulp/paper" whereas the plant is 400,000 adt/yr (Exhibits ES-1, 6-62, 7-3).; (6) Cement plant size is 1.3 M t/yr in ES-1 and case exhibits but 1.29 M t in Exhibits 7-3/7-4; iron/steel O&M Exhibit 6-52 gives 2.5 M t steel/yr vs 2.54 elsewhere.; (7) MEA defined as "Monoethanethiol" in the acronym list and Section 3.3 (should be monoethanolamine).; (8) Heating-value basis of the natural gas MMBtu consumption is not stated.; (9) Section 3.1.2.4 cross-reference to the NG price sensitivity section is missing ("Section 7.2.3 and Section respectively"), and "Section 0" broken cross-references appear (pp.8, 10, 39).; (10) Greenfield pulp cases carry zero purchased power and fuel cost (energy from base plant), so their COC is not comparable to the other low-purity cases without the base-plant derate.; (11) Capture system costs carry a vendor accuracy range of -25/+40% (p.4), not propagated to the tables.
